chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Zurara, who said:

I found in the Parchment of Inheritance Shares that a man died and left behind his daughter and his two parents, so for the daughter is three shares, and for the two parents, for each one of them is one share. The wealth is divided into five parts, so whatever amount constitutes three parts belongs to the daughter, and whatever amount constitutes two parts belongs to the two parents.
ai.seo_question: How is an estate divided when a man dies leaving only his daughter and both parents?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the 'Sab' al-Muwassalah' (the connected inheritance) scenario where a daughter and both parents inherit simultaneously, a case often discussed in Shia jurisprudence regarding the balance between fixed shares (fard) and residual portions (residuary). The text explicitly details the division of the estate into five parts, assigning three to the daughter and one to each parent, reflecting the specific application of Quranic verses in the presence of multiple heirs. This specific distribution underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on precise arithmetic allocation in inheritance law, distinguishing it from other schools that might apply different rules for the parents' share in the presence of a daughter.
